subject: SIG: data supply-chain inventory & telemetry endpoints request
messages:
From: security@brightlanehealth.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightlanehealth.com
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 16:14:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: inventory of downstream services and telemetry endpoints

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for agreeing to run through the SIG intake for Brightlane's vendor assessment. Our external risk team needs a consolidated inventory of Redwood's downstream data consumers (subprocessors) and telemetry/monitoring endpoints that receive production logs or metrics for our SOC 2 review. Specifically we need: 1) a list of all subprocessors (name, service type, region, contact), 2) the purpose of each (telemetry, storage, analytics, support), 3) data types transmitted (tokens, logs, telemetry), and 4) any outbound network endpoints (FQDNs/IP ranges) used for telemetry or error reporting.

Can you provide an initial inventory and an ETA? Preferably as an XLSX or CSV so our intake system can ingest it.

Appreciate it — we are aiming to complete vendor evidence collection by Dec 10 to align with our SOC 2 audit runbook.

— Alex Morgan
Brightlane Health — Security Engineering
security@brightlanehealth.com
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: security@brightlanehealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: inventory of downstream services and telemetry endpoints

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We can get you a draft export with the fields you requested. High-level plan:

- Marissa will pull our canonical subprocessor registry and map services to purpose tags (telemetry, storage, support, infra)
- Karthik will validate cloud regions and any contracts that affect data residency
- I will assemble the outbound endpoint list from our egress rules and ops runbooks

ETA: Draft spreadsheet by EOD Monday (Dec 6), final by Dec 8.

Two quick clarifying questions: 1) do you need historical versions / effective dates for each subprocessor (we can include contract effective date column), and 2) are telemetry recipients limited to services that receive production logs (vs. internal metrics collectors for ops)?

If you want a narrower scope, let me know and we can trim columns.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: security@brightlanehealth.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: inventory of downstream services and telemetry endpoints (draft)

Alex — attaching the draft inventory as requested. Summary notes included in the first tab. High-level items to call out:

- Cloud providers: AWS (us-west-2 primary), GCP (us-east1 for embeddings pipeline), Azure (backup in eu-west) — purpose column included.
- Telemetry recipients: Datadog (metrics/traces), Sentry (error reporting), Honeycomb (high-cardinality observability), internal aggregation service (redwood-ops-telemetry) — see telemetry_flag column.
- Support tools: Zendesk (support tickets), Intercom (in-app messaging) — these receive non-production ticket data unless a customer attaches logs.

Attachments: redwood_sig_subprocessor_inventory_v1.xlsx (contains: name, service_type, purpose, region, contact, contract_effective_date, data_types, telemetry_flag, outbound_endpoints)

Notes: We left IP ranges blank for third parties where they rotate via CDN; for those we've listed FQDNs and suggested firewall rules. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through.

— Marissa Cole
Program Manager, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_sig_subprocessor_inventory_v1.xlsx
From: security@brightlanehealth.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightlanehealth.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: inventory of downstream services and telemetry endpoints (clarifications)

Marissa/Vivek — received, thanks. Quick clarifications from our intake team:

1) For services flagged telemetry_flag = true, can you separate which receive PII/PHI-derived telemetry (we only accept telemetry containing no PHI unless a BAA is in place)?
2) For cloud providers listed as "backup" or "edge", please provide the specific bucket/namespace names or project IDs so we can match to our dataflow scan.
3) For any third parties that store logs >90 days, please call that out (retention column).

If easier, we can accept a follow-up sheet that only includes telemetry recipients and retention/PII columns.

Thanks — Alex
Brightlane Security
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: security@brightlanehealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: inventory of downstream services and telemetry endpoints (final deliverable)

Alex — attaching the trimmed telemetry-only sheet and a network dataflow map. Key answers inline:

- PII/PHI in telemetry: None of our standard telemetry collectors receive raw customer PHI. Exceptions: our support upload pipeline can ingest customer-provided logs (marked in support_uploads column) — those entries are flagged and require a separate BAA before retention >30 days.
- Bucket/project identifiers: Provided for GCP projects and AWS bucket names in the second tab; Azure backup namespaces redwood-azure-backups-eu listed.
- Retention: Anything >90 days is explicitly flagged (logging_retention column).

Attachments: redwood_sig_subprocessor_inventory_v1.xlsx (updated: telemetry-only tab), redwood_network_dataflow_map.png

Request: please confirm whether this format satisfies Brightlane's intake and if you want a signed attestation for any BAAs referenced.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
